baseline: 10 of 12 new cases failed on the unpatched upstream source.
hypothesis: Benign exit notes should not name commands that may never have run.
intervention: Quote-aware attribution only for unambiguous single commands.
limitations: No hidden shell status is reconstructed; existing upstream PR 94360 overlaps this issue.
regression: Simple grep notes and signal cases passed.
result: 42 focused tests passed on the integrated branch; 14 lint and health checks passed.

baseline: Seven new recovery cases failed before the patch; a target-resolution case was also red.
hypothesis: Surface observed missing commands, target-resolution errors and recoverable syntax failures without changing the shell status.
intervention: Bounded, advisory terminal hints; no retries or scans.
limitations: Pattern evidence can be quoted output and is advisory.
regression: Read/log-display heads and inert quoted separators remain unannotated in tests.
result: 46 focused tests passed; one platform-specific test skipped. Real Hermes terminal registry dispatch preserved exit 0 and surfaced a missing-command hint.

baseline: The prior local prompt omitted effective UID and shell; two new native macOS checks failed.
hypothesis: Explicit effective identity and platform hints reduce ambiguity about the local tool environment.
intervention: Add local identity, shell and macOS notes to the existing session-start environment block.
limitations: No model-level causality claim; remote execution identity remains unknown unless separately probed.
regression: Remote backend tests show no local identity or home directory leakage.
result: 60 focused tests passed; one platform-specific test skipped.

baseline: A synthetic 65,536-token custom-model config was inspected as 256,000 tokens.
hypothesis: Offline prompt inspection should use the configured default-model context pin.
intervention: Restore the configured pin on the disposable offline inspection agent.
limitations: The initial fallback warning may still be logged before restoration; no live agent or model was modified.
regression: The no-pin custom endpoint remains unprobed.
result: Six focused tests passed, including local custom and smaller LM Studio-style contexts with blocked socket connections.

baseline: The capability did not exist in this package.
hypothesis: The native plugin can attach evidence and expose a synthetic Entra capability without network or model calls.
intervention: Versioned evidence hook, FTS5 knowledge cards, deterministic assessment and truth-table reconciliation.
limitations: No production installation, tenant access or autonomous live-chat routing.
regression: Unknown or malformed outputs do not establish success; original result fields stay intact.
result: Native plugin doctor and isolated real Hermes dispatch/hook probe passed.

baseline: Fresh in-memory FTS5 index for every query.
hypothesis: Content-validated per-thread index caching reduces repeated retrieval overhead without changing answers.
intervention: Content-hashed invalidation with bounded per-thread result caching.
limitations: Three tiny project-authored cards, warm local process; not a model or end-to-end speed measurement.
regression: Tested same-size same-mtime edits, cross-thread results and returned-object mutation.
result: Nine alternating samples of 1,500 queries each: medians 195.7 vs 51.9 microseconds/query, 3.8x. Tested query results matched exactly.

baseline: Local Qwythos v2 MTP Q4, CPU-only, four synthetic per-policy questions, same policy facts and explicit rules.
hypothesis: A deterministic policy tool can answer a narrow class faster without losing the verdict.
intervention: Already-selected Hermes deterministic tool with source facts and reconciliation.
limitations: Four cases; excludes process startup and tool-selection decision; direct model calls compared to tool dispatch, not faster model inference.
regression: Both paths returned the same expected verdicts on this fixed sample.
result: Model 4/4, tool 4/4 and evidence 4/4. Total model calls 22,915.6 ms; tool dispatch 34.7 ms, approximately 661x.

baseline: The same local model and five additional synthetic cases with explicit scope instructions.
hypothesis: The tool should return indeterminate on unsupported or ambiguous controls rather than guess.
intervention: Already-selected deterministic tool and independent truth-table reconciliation.
limitations: Five additional exploratory cases; excludes startup and tool selection.
regression: All five synthetic tool verdicts matched the preregistered expected result.
result: Model 3/5, tool 5/5 and evidence 5/5. Model calls 40,434.2 ms; tool dispatch 34.3 ms.

baseline: Only four admitted original synthetic examples; no actual post-fix held-out model baseline.
hypothesis: Qwythos tool-use LoRA improves residual failures after deterministic fixes.
intervention: Candidate rank-8 full-attention q/v projection adapter; not trained.
limitations: No weights downloaded for the feasibility audit, no training, no adapter promotion.
result: Checkpoint architecture, tensor names and published weights/license verified by metadata and bounded tensor-header reads; train/serve compatibility and fit remain unverified.

baseline: Direct local Qwythos CPU model calls on nine previously seen synthetic cases, with the same facts and explicit conservative decision instructions.
hypothesis: A narrow caller-invoked deterministic route can avoid local model calls while preserving the explicitly specified single-policy verdicts.
intervention: Time the routing predicate, real Hermes dispatch and hardened source, scope, remediation and truth-table evidence checks.
limitations: Repeat confirmation, not a new independent holdout; synthetic fixtures only, caller supplies fixture and policy ID. Excludes startup, arbitrary request entity extraction and production integration. Not model-inference acceleration or a general quality guarantee. Network use was not instrumented.
regression: All nine specified route outcomes and evidence checks matched; mutation and tampering regressions passed separately.
result: Model 7/9; routed tool 9/9; evidence 9/9. Total model time 79,929.4 ms; route 57.1 ms; approximately 1,401x for the sum. Owned model-server child stopped.
